name: Andesine
physical: Linked to a warm, energized feeling
Kept nearby for stamina on busy days
summary: Andesine is a warm red, orange or green feldspar from the plagioclase series, loved for courage, vitality and a bright, sun-kissed spirit. Warm and lively.
intro: Andesine is a plagioclase feldspar that sits between albite and anorthite on the sodium-calcium scale, and it is best known today for its sunny red, orange, and green faceted gems. The color is rarely natural in the vivid shades seen in jewelry shops, because many of the stones are copper-diffused: a heat process pushes copper into the feldspar to create the reds and greens. Natural andesine often looks pale yellow, brown, or greyish. Fine natural stones come from the Congo, while treated stones are widely traded from Tibet and Inner Mongolia, though the source of some of this material has been controversial. The glassy, glowing color makes it a lively collectors' gem.
history: Andesine takes its name from the Andes Mountains, where it was first described from a volcanic rock called andesite in 1841. For many decades it was only a rock-forming mineral, appearing in diorite and andesite, and rarely used as a gem. In the early 2000s, vivid red and green andesine appeared on the market labeled as Tibetan or Mongolian material and was marketed as natural. Later testing showed that much of it was copper-diffused, and the trade learned to disclose the treatment. Natural andesine from the Congo and Tanzania has also been used as sunstone-like material, which has made the name confusing in the market.
meaning: In the crystal tradition andesine is a stone of warmth and courage. Its fiery colors are linked to the Sacral and Solar Plexus chakras, and the stone is used to bring energy, confidence, and a sunnier outlook. People turn to it when they feel timid or low on drive, saying it helps them step forward. Red andesine is associated with passion and motivation, while green is linked to the Heart and with gentle growth. Because many stones on the market are treated, practitioners often say it is the intention, not the origin, that matters most to them. It is a lovely companion for new ventures, creative projects, and anyone starting something that needs a spark.
howToUse: Wear a faceted andesine ring or pendant to carry its bright color with you. Hold a stone during morning meditation and imagine warm light filling your belly. Place one on your desk to support motivation while working on a project. In a grid, use it with carnelian and sunstone for an energy and courage layout. Green andesine can sit near the heart with green aventurine for gentle growth. Some people gift andesine to a friend starting a new venture as a token of encouragement.
care: Andesine is Mohs 6 to 6.5 with feldspar cleavage, so protect it from knocks and store it separately from harder gems. A quick lukewarm rinse is fine, but avoid long soaks and ultrasonic cleaners. Treated copper-diffused stones should be kept away from harsh chemicals and strong heat. Cleanse with sound, smoke, or moonlight. Sunlight is generally safe, but avoid hot cars or heaters. Wipe with a soft cloth.
identify: Natural andesine is usually pale yellow, brown, or colorless, so very vivid red or green faceted stones are almost always copper-diffused. Reputable sellers disclose this. Glass imitations show bubbles and swirl marks, while true andesine shows twinning lines under magnification. It can be confused with sunstone, labradorite, and red or green glass. A lab report is the surest way to know whether color is natural or treated.

faq.a: Andesine is a natural mineral, but much of the vivid red and green gem material is copper-diffused to create its color. Natural andesine is usually paler yellow or brown. Ask sellers whether a stone is treated.
Andesine is traditionally used for courage, vitality, and warmth. People keep it near for motivation and a brighter mood, and link it to the Sacral and Solar Plexus chakras.

faq.q: How do I care for andesine?
faq.a: Rinse briefly in lukewarm water, dry it well, and avoid ultrasonic cleaners or heat. Andesine has cleavage and can chip, so store it apart from harder stones and wear it in earrings or pendants more than rings.
